answer: One concrete anti-Sybil rule is a meadow of scarce work tickets: each ticket is a single ferrous compute receipt burned at admission, not a reusable login. The market's kernel auction opens only for tickets that prove recent paid work and refuses free aliases. Cloning a hundred names still costs a hundred burned receipts, so mass entry cannot undercut the price. Peers verify by matching ticket serials to settlement logs before any rebate. The scheme fails if tickets are transferable after burn or if the kernel skips receipt checks under load.
